summary: Tested the new AI Writing Coach feature end-to-end. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_writing_coach.py (15 pytest cases) covering POST /api/ai/proofread (messy/clean/empty/invalid/auth, exact-substring guarantee, punctuation+capitalization detection), GET/PUT /api/studio/writing-gate (route ordering vs /studio/{track_id}, guide-only 403, explorer inheritance, 422 validation) and submit->reports writing_flag lifecycle (set + clear). All 15 passed. Frontend (Playwright, explorer em-exp / guide em-guide): Docs check-writing dialog + squigglies, Docs HARD HALT (blocks submit, halt note visible, no grade dialog; grades after fixes), Email compose check-writing + squigglies, Email HARD HALT + reading-pane squigglies, guide gate toggle ON/OFF with persistence, gate-OFF submit proceeds and shows red 'Writing issues' flag (writing-flag-em-exp-docs) in Guide Reports, and guide grade-preview correctly bypasses the writing gate (no check-writing buttons for guides). One real functional defect found: Apply fix / Apply all fixes replaces the wrong text when the flagged substring also occurs earlier in the document.

ui_bugs.issue: Apply fix replaces the FIRST block whose text .includes(issue.text), not the block/offset the issue actually came from. Reproduced: left starter blocks untouched, typed 'i dont like it' into the LAST block, ran Submit (gate ON) -> Apply all fixes. Result: block 1 'My First Document' was corrupted to 'My FIrst Document' while the real error stayed as 'i don't like it'. Re-submitting then halts again (now flagging 'FIrst'), so the student is bounced repeatedly AND the mission's graded text (task 'Bold the title line (My First Document)') is damaged. Root cause: getDocText() joins header + all blocks into one string so per-issue character offsets are lost; applyIssueToDoc then does a blind first-match .replace(). Fix: proofread per block (or carry the joined-text offset and map back to block+index) and use word-boundary matching.

Issues are matched with plain substring .includes(), so a short flagged token underlines letters inside unrelated words/blocks. Reproduced: issue text 'i' produced squigglies in 'A quick tour of the editor' and 'Click any line above...' (3 squigglies for 1 issue). Needs word-boundary/offset-aware matching.

Possible race observed once: the mount GET /studio/writing-gate resolved after an early toggle click and reset the Switch back to ON while the backend had persisted OFF (toast said 'turned off', switch still data-state=checked). Not reproducible after reload. Suggest ignoring the stale GET (or disabling the toggle until loaded).

issues: The checker proofreads the mission's seeded starter text (header + all pre-filled blocks), not just what the student wrote, so with hard-halt ON a student can be blocked by curriculum text they never typed. Consider limiting the check to student-edited content.

action_items: Fix apply-fix targeting: proofread per block (or map joined-text offsets back to block + char index) so Apply fix / Apply all edits the exact occurrence; add word-boundary matching to avoid corrupting unrelated words (HIGH — corrupts graded mission text and creates a repeat hard-halt loop).
Make computeSegments / DocEditorCore issue filtering offset- or word-boundary-based so short tokens ('i', 'no') stop underlining letters inside unrelated words.
Guard the ReportsTab gate Switch against the stale initial GET overwriting a just-toggled value.
critical_code_review_comments: StudioMission.getDocText() flattens header + blocks (and table cells) into one string, discarding the mapping needed by applyIssueToDoc — this is the root cause of the wrong-block replacement.
applyIssueToDoc uses String.replace(issue.text, suggestion) on the first matching field; use an index-based splice on the known block/offset instead.
applyFix drops issues by object identity (arr.filter(i => i !== issue)); works today because review.issues and docIssues share objects, but is fragile — prefer a stable issue id/index.

Backend /api/ai/proofread correctly validates that each issue.text is a verbatim substring and fails open on LLM errors — good. Gate route is declared before /studio/{track_id}, verified not shadowed.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (all gate/halt/flag flows pass; apply-fix targeting defective)

Left one deliberate flagged submission: studio_progress em-exp/docs-m2 unresolved_writing=6 (drives the red 'Writing issues' flag in Guide Reports). writing_gate setting for em-guide restored to ON (true).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_writing_coach.py (15 pass, ~17s, live Claude). Frontend flows verified via cookie injection on https://explorer-journey-4.preview.emergentagent.com: /studio/docs/docs-m1 (check + hard halt + apply all + grade), /studio/email/email-m3 (compose check, send, hard halt, sent-pane squigglies), /guide > Reports (writing-gate-toggle, writing-flag-em-exp-docs). Retest focus after fix: apply-fix must edit only the flagged occurrence — repro is to type errors ONLY in the last block and leave the seeded 'My First Document' first block untouched, then Apply all.
rca_of_the_issue: StudioMission concatenates the header and every block into a single string for proofreading, so the returned issues carry only a text snippet with no position. applyIssueToDoc then searches blocks in order and rewrites the first field containing that snippet, so a snippet that also appears earlier (e.g. the letter 'i' inside 'First') is replaced in the wrong place, leaving the actual error unfixed and mutating graded starter text. The same substring-only matching in Squiggly.computeSegments / DocEditorCore causes false-positive underlines.
